title: GPU fleet surge mitigation and graceful degradation for tenant throughput guarantees
creator: Rohan Patel
description: Problem: Dedicated customers require firm throughput guarantees even under tenant surge scenarios. Current behavior: when a tenant suddenly increases request volume, adjacent tenants on shared pools experience latency spikes or dropped requests. Objective: introduce a multi-tiered surge mitigation system that enforces per-tenant contractual throughput while enabling graceful degradation for best-effort tenants and autoscaling-triggerable fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) During synthetic surge tests (50x baseline qps for 30s), SLA-backed tenants maintain >=95% of their committed throughput and p95 latency within 1.5x baseline.
2) Best-effort tenants are throttled down deterministically using token-bucket backpressure to prevent downstream latency degradation for SLA tenants.
3) Autoscale triggers for Dedicated pools fire within 60s of sustained overload and increase capacity to restore baseline throughput within defined hysteresis windows.
4) No silent failures: all throttles, evictions, and autoscale events are recorded in the Console and exposed via per-tenant audit logs and metrics.
5) End-to-end canary rollout with on-call guardrails completed and rollback playbook validated in staging.
6) All new configuration knobs are documented in the Console with sensible defaults and secure RBAC controls.
design_decisions: Use a hierarchical quota model: guaranteed committed throughput (hard contract) > soft quota (best-effort) > burst reservoir (time-limited credits).
Enforce enforcement at the lane scheduler level rather than per-GPU process to preserve kernel-level batching efficiency.
Prefer cooperative throttling (token-bucket + 429/503 with Retry-After) over aggressive eviction where possible; evictions reserved for persistent contract violations.
Autoscale policy will be predictive + reactive: short-term reactive scale-up (fast path) and predictive smoothing using 5m rolling trend for scale-down to avoid flapping.
Telemetry surface includes per-tenant throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token-bucket fill level, burst credits remaining, and autoscale decision traces.
implementation_notes: Scheduler changes: introduce a tenant-aware reservation table with per-lane token-bucket accounting and credit decay timed at 1s granularity.
KV cache and batching implications: when a tenant is throttled, preserve KV cache entries to avoid warm-up penalties on unthrottled tenants sharing models.
Eviction flow: mark processes for soft-quiesce -> attempt graceful draining for 10s -> hard-evict if still over quota, emitting detailed reason codes.
Autoscaler hooks: add a short-lived fast-path scale API that can provision spare nodes in under 75s for common GPU types; integrate with cost controls to respect reserved capacity commitments.
Config surface: Console exposes per-tenant committed qps, burst window seconds, and autoscale priority (low/normal/high). Defaults: burst_window=30s, burst_credits=3x baseline.
Backward compatibility: fallback to current lane behavior if new token accounting is disabled per pool.
benchmarks_and_spike_results: Staging synthetic test: 100-tenant mixed workload with one tenant surge to 60x baseline for 45s. Observed: committed tenants kept 97% throughput, median p95 latency multiple 1.3x baseline.
Eviction test: configured two persistent violators; soft-quiesce succeeded 88% of the time without hard-eviction. Hard-eviction path restores headroom within 12s on average.
Autoscale latency: provisioning measured at 68s for A100 pools with fast-path API during pre-warmed workflow; cold-path 140s.
Cost delta: enabling burst reservoirs increased short-term GPU usage by ~6% under heavy synthetic surges; predictive scale-down recovered cost within 12m on average.
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket accounting and decay logic.
Integration tests for scheduler-level enforcement preserving batching across lanes.
Chaos tests simulating flapping tenants and partial network partitions; verify graceful degradation and no silent data loss.
Performance regression tests measuring p50/p95/p99 on mixed workloads pre/post change.
Canary rollout in dedicated-staging with traffic mirroring for one enterprise customer cluster before broad rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge feature flags behind pool-level opt-in and deploy to staging clusters (done).
Phase 2: Enabled for low-risk Dedicated pools and run 48h soak with synthetic surges; collect metrics and iterate (current).
Phase 3: Controlled canary for two enterprise customers with on-call monitoring and quick rollback script.
Phase 4: Enable by default with dashboard docs and runbook; deprecate old eviction-only policy after 4 weeks of steady telemetry.
Rollback: immediate disable of token accounting + remove autoscale fast-path if canary shows regressions; pre-written revert PR available (link in links).
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: tenant_committed_throughput, tenant_effective_throughput, tenant_throttle_rate, tenant_burst_credits_remaining.
Alerts: firing if any SLA tenant loses >10% committed throughput for >30s, or if autoscaler fails 3 consecutive provisioning attempts.
Dashboards: per-pool and per-tenant views; Console exposes event stream of throttle and eviction reasons for debugging.
Audit logs: every throttle/eviction/autoscale decision emits an annotated event with correlation_id and responsible-policy.
SLOs: target <1% false-positive evictions; <5% increase in p95 for non-violating tenants when the system is under pressure.
